<reason>A high-quality, genuinely contested debate. A (CON) brought the sharpest single pressure question (the GPS precision standard, which B never numerically answered), cleanly caught B's subrogation answer contradicting B's own "empty wallet" claim, and maintained a real conceptual distinction between funding/compliance duties and fault. But B (PRO) held the decisive frame all debate: the motion says "more" responsibility, not "all," and B's flipped analogies (the operator never loses control at handover; the dashboard beats the bartender) were never squarely beaten. B's closing landed the two most damaging late moves: co-opting A's own per-ride insurance pool as "the motion, conceded and renamed," and answering A's "speed, not aim" line with accurate kinetic-energy physics ("injuries are made of speed"). A's counter-reversal (cars as heavier energy) overstated B's actual proposal — B had specified half-block 8 mph caps, not "walking speed" districts — which blunted it. A also absorbed two execution costs via clipped turns. B's blemishes (the precision duck, a nonexistent [C2.x] reference) were real but smaller than the ground A surrendered on prevention and framing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The decisive exchange ran from A's Rebuttal 2 ("a throttle changes speed, not aim") into B's Closing: B answered with v-squared energy math (8 mph ≈ a third the energy of 15 mph — "a bruise instead of a broken hip"), converting A's causation point into B's prevention win, then paired it with the co-option of A's insurance pool as the motion "conceded and renamed," neutralizing A's two strongest late moves in one speech.</best_rebuttal>
